source.original_text: For all natural d,q with 2q+1<d, put r=q+1, including q=0. On Omega=(R^d)^r with mu the product of r independent standard d-dimensional Gaussian column laws, let Phi_i be the actual physical row. Put theta_i=(i-1/2)pi/d, t_i=(1,sqrt(2)cos(theta_i),...,sqrt(2)cos(q theta_i)), and L=2r+3log(1000d). Define Yi=d^(-1)(Phi_i Phi_i-transpose tensor t_i t_i-transpose) when norm(Phi_i)^2<=L and zero otherwise. The cutoff is inclusive and local to row i. Let Mi be the actual Bochner integral of Yi under this same original unconditional mu, and Zi=Yi-Mi. Matrix measurability uses the standard finite-coordinate Borel structure; norms use real Euclidean operator norms. Each Zi is measurable. The entire family (Zi) indexed by i is jointly independent under mu. Each Zi is Bochner integrable, its actual integral under mu is zero, and Zi(omega) is Hermitian for every i and every omega. These are the structural prerequisites used for the unweighted matrix Bernstein step in Appendix C.2; no concentration tail is asserted here.

blind_reconstruction.text:
For every pair of natural numbers d and q (implicit parameters in Lean), and for every hypothesis hq : 2q + 1 < d, make the following local choices and definitions.

Put I = Fin(q + 1) = {0, ..., q} and J = Fin(d) = {0, ..., d - 1}; an index's numerical value is its zero-based natural-number value. Let M be the real matrix space with both rows and columns indexed by I × I. Fix, as the local measurable-space instance on M, the Borel sigma algebra of its ordinary finite-coordinate topology. The matrix norm convention is the L2 operator norm for the action on real Euclidean spaces; this induces the same topology.

Let D = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), the real d-dimensional Euclidean space, and let E = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin(q + 1)), the real (q + 1)-dimensional Euclidean space. Use their Euclidean norms and Borel sigma algebras. Let Ω = I → D, with its finite product measurable structure, and define the measure

    μ = Measure.pi (b ↦ stdGaussian D),  b ∈ I.

Thus each factor in this displayed product measure is the centered Gaussian probability measure on D with identity covariance. Define the real scalars

    r = (q + 1 : ℕ), coerced to ℝ,
    L = 2r + 3 log(1000 · (d : ℝ)),

where log is the natural logarithm. For every i ∈ J define

    θ(i) = ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - 1/2) · π / (d : ℝ).

For every i ∈ J and k ∈ I define the real-valued function t by

    t(i)(k) = 1                                      if k.val = 0,
              sqrt(2) · cos((k.val : ℝ) · θ(i))       otherwise,

where sqrt is the nonnegative square root. For every i ∈ J and ω ∈ Ω define the Euclidean vector

    row(i, ω) = WithLp.toLp 2 (b ↦ ω(b)(i)) ∈ E.

In particular, its coordinate b is ω(b)(i); WithLp.ofLp(row(i, ω)) is that same coordinate function on I, and its norm is the Euclidean norm on E. Define Y : J → Ω → M by

    Y(i, ω) = (d : ℝ)⁻¹ ·
              [vecMulVec(WithLp.ofLp(row(i, ω)), WithLp.ofLp(row(i, ω)))
               ⊗ vecMulVec(t(i), t(i))]              if ‖row(i, ω)‖² ≤ L,
              0                                     otherwise.

Here 0 is the zero matrix, multiplication by (d : ℝ)⁻¹ is scalar multiplication, vecMulVec(u, v) is the matrix with entry u(a)v(c) at row a and column c, and ⊗ is the Kronecker product. Precisely, for b, c, b′, c′ ∈ I, the entry of Y(i, ω) at row (b, c) and column (b′, c′), when the cutoff holds, is

    (d : ℝ)⁻¹ · ω(b)(i) · ω(b′)(i) · t(i)(c) · t(i)(c′).

When the cutoff fails, all its entries are zero. The cutoff includes equality.

For every i ∈ J define the deterministic matrix

    mean(i) = ∫_Ω Y(i, ω) dμ(ω),

and then define Z : J → Ω → M by

    Z(i, ω) = Y(i, ω) - mean(i).

These integrals are Bochner integrals, with the Lean convention that the integral is zero when the integrand is not integrable. The definition of mean uses this totalized integral.

With exactly these local definitions, the following five claims hold together:

1. For every i ∈ J, the function ω ↦ Z(i, ω) is measurable from Ω with its displayed product measurable structure into M with the locally fixed Borel sigma algebra.
2. The entire indexed family (ω ↦ Z(i, ω)) indexed by i ∈ J is jointly independent under μ, in the sense of iIndepFun Z μ.
3. For every i ∈ J, the function ω ↦ Z(i, ω) is Bochner integrable with respect to μ: it is almost everywhere strongly measurable and the integral of its matrix norm is finite.
4. For every i ∈ J, its Bochner integral is the zero matrix:

       ∫_Ω Z(i, ω) dμ(ω) = 0.

5. For every i ∈ J and every ω ∈ Ω, the real matrix Z(i, ω) is Hermitian. Equivalently, it equals its transpose; in entries, Z(i, ω)[(b, c), (b′, c′)] = Z(i, ω)[(b′, c′), (b, c)] for every b, c, b′, c′ ∈ I.

All the definitions and the five conclusions lie inside the scope of the initial quantifiers on d, q, and hq. The parameter range allows q = 0. The hypothesis forces d ≥ 2q + 2, hence d ≥ 2, so J and I are nonempty and the displayed real denominator d is nonzero. The final symmetry claim is pointwise for every sample ω, while the asserted integrability has its usual almost-everywhere strong-measurability component.

integrability, independence, zero-mean and Hermitian obligations are discharged
internally under the sole original source condition. -/
noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped BigOperators Matrix Kronecker Matrix.Norms.L2Operator
set_option autoImplicit false
namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumSourceMatrixStructure

theorem actual_source_centered_matrix_structure
    {d q : ℕ} (hq : 2 * q + 1 < d) :
  letI : MeasurableSpace
      (Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ) :=
    borel (Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ)
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q + 1))
  let Ω := Fin (q + 1) → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (q + 1) => stdGaussian D)
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let t : Fin d → Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun b : Fin (q + 1) => ω b i)
  let Y : Fin d → Ω →
      Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ := fun i ω =>
    if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)) (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
    else 0
  let mean : Fin d → Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ :=
    fun i => ∫ ω, Y i ω ∂μ
  let Z : Fin d → Ω → Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ :=
    fun i ω => Y i ω - mean i
  (∀ i : Fin d, Measurable (Z i)) ∧
    iIndepFun Z μ ∧
    (∀ i : Fin d, Integrable (Z i) μ) ∧
    (∀ i : Fin d, (∫ ω, Z i ω ∂μ) = 0) ∧
    (∀ i : Fin d, ∀ ω : Ω, (Z i ω).IsHermitian)
 := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let : MeasurableSpace
      (Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ) :=
    borel (Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ)
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q + 1))
  let Ω := Fin (q + 1) → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (q + 1) => stdGaussian D)
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let t : Fin d → Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun b : Fin (q + 1) => ω b i)
  let Y : Fin d → Ω →
      Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ := fun i ω =>
    if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)) (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
    else 0
  let mean : Fin d → Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ :=
    fun i => ∫ ω, Y i ω ∂μ
  let Z : Fin d → Ω → Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ :=
    fun i ω => Y i ω - mean i
  let : BorelSpace (Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ) := ⟨rfl⟩

  let : IsProbabilityMeasure μ := by dsimp only [μ]; infer_instance
  change (∀ i : Fin d, Measurable (Z i)) ∧ iIndepFun Z μ ∧
    (∀ i : Fin d, Integrable (Z i) μ) ∧
    (∀ i : Fin d, (∫ ω, Z i ω ∂μ) = 0) ∧
    (∀ i : Fin d, ∀ ω : Ω, (Z i ω).IsHermitian)
  let F : Fin d → E → Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1))
      (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ := fun i x =>
    if ‖x‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec x.ofLp x.ofLp) (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
    else 0
  have row_law (i : Fin d) : MeasurePreserving (row i) μ (stdGaussian E) :=
    FixedSpectrumSourceRowLaw.actual_source_row_marginal_law hq i
  have row_independent : iIndepFun row μ :=
    FixedSpectrumSourceRowIndependence.actual_source_rows_independent hq
  have cutoff : MeasurableSet {x : E | ‖x‖ ^ 2 ≤ L} :=
    measurableSet_le (by fun_prop) measurable_const
  have coordinate (k : Fin (q + 1)) : Continuous (fun x : E => x k) := by
    dsimp [E]
    fun_prop
  have F_measurable (i : Fin d) : Measurable (F i) := by
    apply Measurable.ite cutoff
    · apply Continuous.measurable
      apply continuous_pi
      intro u
      apply continuous_pi
      intro v
      change Continuous (fun x : E =>
        (d : ℝ)⁻¹ * ((x u.1 * x v.1) * (t i u.2 * t i v.2)))
      exact continuous_const.mul
        (((coordinate u.1).mul (coordinate v.1)).mul continuous_const)
    · exact measurable_const
  have translated_measurable (i : Fin d) :
      Measurable (fun x : E => F i x - mean i) :=
    (F_measurable i).sub measurable_const
  have Z_measurable (i : Fin d) : Measurable (Z i) :=
    (translated_measurable i).comp (row_law i).measurable
  have Z_independent : iIndepFun Z μ :=
    row_independent.comp (fun i x => F i x - mean i) translated_measurable
  let a : ℝ := (∫ x : E, Set.indicator {y : E | ‖y‖ ^ 2 ≤ L}
    (fun y : E => ‖y‖ ^ 2) x ∂stdGaussian E) / r
  have hm := FixedSpectrumSourceMatrixMean.actual_source_truncated_matrix_means
    (d := d) (q := q) hq
  change (∀ i : Fin d, Integrable (Y i) μ) ∧
    (∀ i : Fin d, mean i = (a / (d : ℝ)) • Matrix.kronecker
      (1 : Matrix (Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1)) ℝ)
      (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))) at hm
  have Y_hermitian (i : Fin d) (ω : Ω) : (Y i ω).IsHermitian := by
    change (Y i ω).conjTranspose = Y i ω
    by_cases hx : ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L
    · ext u v
      simp only [Y, if_pos hx, Matrix.conjTranspose_apply, Matrix.smul_apply,
        Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply, Matrix.vecMulVec_apply,
        smul_eq_mul, star_trivial]
      ring
    · simp [Y, hx]
  have mean_hermitian (i : Fin d) : (mean i).IsHermitian := by
    rw [hm.2 i]
    change ((a / (d : ℝ)) • Matrix.kronecker
      (1 : Matrix (Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1)) ℝ)
      (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))).conjTranspose = _
    ext u v
    simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_apply, Matrix.one_apply, Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.kroneckerMap,
      Matrix.vecMulVec, eq_comm, mul_comm]
  have Z_integrable (i : Fin d) : Integrable (Z i) μ :=
    (hm.1 i).sub (integrable_const _)
  have Z_mean_zero (i : Fin d) : (∫ ω, Z i ω ∂μ) = 0 := by
    change (∫ ω, Y i ω - mean i ∂μ) = 0
    rw [integral_sub (hm.1 i) (integrable_const _)]
    simp [mean]
  exact ⟨Z_measurable, Z_independent, Z_integrable, Z_mean_zero,
    fun i ω => (Y_hermitian i ω).sub (mean_hermitian i)⟩

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumSourceMatrixStructure

Matrices have the standard finite-coordinate Borel structure and real Euclidean operator norm topology. The local Lean measurable-space definition fixes this standard structure; it is not a caller-supplied assumption.

The only proposition input is \(2q+1<d\). Measurability, integrability, independence, actual centering and symmetry are proved internally. In the private consumer \(X_i=w_iZ_i\), \(w_i=\cos((2q+1)\theta_i)\) may be zero or negative.

  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let t : Fin d → Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun b : Fin (q + 1) => ω b i)
  let Y : Fin d → Ω →
      Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ := fun i ω =>
    if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)) (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
    else 0
  let mean : Fin d → Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ :=
    fun i => ∫ ω, Y i ω ∂μ
  let Z : Fin d → Ω → Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ :=
    fun i ω => Y i ω - mean i
  let : BorelSpace (Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ) := ⟨rfl⟩

  let : IsProbabilityMeasure μ := by dsimp only [μ]; infer_instance
  change (∀ i : Fin d, Measurable (Z i)) ∧ iIndepFun Z μ ∧
    (∀ i : Fin d, Integrable (Z i) μ) ∧
    (∀ i : Fin d, (∫ ω, Z i ω ∂μ) = 0) ∧
    (∀ i : Fin d, ∀ ω : Ω, (Z i ω).IsHermitian)

steps.title: Transport row independence through the measurable truncated map
steps.text: The canonical row law supplies measurability of each physical row, and the canonical joint row law supplies independence of the whole row family. The closed squared-radius event is measurable and every tensor coordinate is a continuous polynomial in the row coordinates. Subtracting a fixed actual mean gives an index-specific measurable map; joint independence is preserved under these separate maps.
steps.formula: F_i(x)=d^{-1}(xx^\top\otimes t_it_i^\top)\mathbf1_{\{\|x\|^2\le L\}},\quad Z_i=F_i(\Phi_i)-M_i,\quad(\Phi_i)_i\text{ independent}\Longrightarrow(Z_i)_i\text{ independent}.
steps.lean:
let F : Fin d → E → Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1))
      (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ := fun i x =>
    if ‖x‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec x.ofLp x.ofLp) (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
    else 0
  have row_law (i : Fin d) : MeasurePreserving (row i) μ (stdGaussian E) :=
    FixedSpectrumSourceRowLaw.actual_source_row_marginal_law hq i
  have row_independent : iIndepFun row μ :=
    FixedSpectrumSourceRowIndependence.actual_source_rows_independent hq
  have cutoff : MeasurableSet {x : E | ‖x‖ ^ 2 ≤ L} :=
    measurableSet_le (by fun_prop) measurable_const
  have coordinate (k : Fin (q + 1)) : Continuous (fun x : E => x k) := by
    dsimp [E]
    fun_prop
  have F_measurable (i : Fin d) : Measurable (F i) := by
    apply Measurable.ite cutoff
    · apply Continuous.measurable
      apply continuous_pi
      intro u
      apply continuous_pi
      intro v
      change Continuous (fun x : E =>
        (d : ℝ)⁻¹ * ((x u.1 * x v.1) * (t i u.2 * t i v.2)))
      exact continuous_const.mul
        (((coordinate u.1).mul (coordinate v.1)).mul continuous_const)
    · exact measurable_const
  have translated_measurable (i : Fin d) :
      Measurable (fun x : E => F i x - mean i) :=
    (F_measurable i).sub measurable_const
  have Z_measurable (i : Fin d) : Measurable (Z i) :=
    (translated_measurable i).comp (row_law i).measurable
  have Z_independent : iIndepFun Z μ :=
    row_independent.comp (fun i x => F i x - mean i) translated_measurable

steps.title: Use the actual integrable mean and prove pointwise symmetry
steps.text: The existing actual-mean theorem gives genuine integrability of Yi and its radial formula. Real outer products and their tensor product are symmetric on the retained branch; outside it Yi is zero. The evaluated mean is also symmetric, so centering preserves self-adjointness. This chooses the radial-mean route; a separate direct integral-symmetry route is not an extra requirement.
steps.formula: a=\frac1r\int_{\mathbb R^r}\|x\|^2\mathbf1_{\{\|x\|^2\le L\}}\,d\gamma_r,\qquad M_i=\frac ad(I_r\otimes t_it_i^\top),\qquad Y_i^\top=Y_i,\quad M_i^\top=M_i.
steps.lean:
let a : ℝ := (∫ x : E, Set.indicator {y : E | ‖y‖ ^ 2 ≤ L}
    (fun y : E => ‖y‖ ^ 2) x ∂stdGaussian E) / r
  have hm := FixedSpectrumSourceMatrixMean.actual_source_truncated_matrix_means
    (d := d) (q := q) hq
  change (∀ i : Fin d, Integrable (Y i) μ) ∧
    (∀ i : Fin d, mean i = (a / (d : ℝ)) • Matrix.kronecker
      (1 : Matrix (Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1)) ℝ)
      (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))) at hm
  have Y_hermitian (i : Fin d) (ω : Ω) : (Y i ω).IsHermitian := by
    change (Y i ω).conjTranspose = Y i ω
    by_cases hx : ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L
    · ext u v
      simp only [Y, if_pos hx, Matrix.conjTranspose_apply, Matrix.smul_apply,
        Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply, Matrix.vecMulVec_apply,
        smul_eq_mul, star_trivial]
      ring
    · simp [Y, hx]
  have mean_hermitian (i : Fin d) : (mean i).IsHermitian := by
    rw [hm.2 i]
    change ((a / (d : ℝ)) • Matrix.kronecker
      (1 : Matrix (Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1)) ℝ)
      (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))).conjTranspose = _
    ext u v
    simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_apply, Matrix.one_apply, Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.kroneckerMap,
      Matrix.vecMulVec, eq_comm, mul_comm]

steps.title: Prove true zero mean under the original probability
steps.text: Subtracting a constant from the already integrable Yi proves integrability of Zi. Since the original measure is a probability, the integral of the constant Mi is Mi. Bochner linearity therefore gives the actual zero-mean identity. Combine this with measurability, joint independence and pointwise symmetry.
steps.lean:
have Z_integrable (i : Fin d) : Integrable (Z i) μ :=
    (hm.1 i).sub (integrable_const _)
  have Z_mean_zero (i : Fin d) : (∫ ω, Z i ω ∂μ) = 0 := by
    change (∫ ω, Y i ω - mean i ∂μ) = 0
    rw [integral_sub (hm.1 i) (integrable_const _)]
    simp [mean]
  exact ⟨Z_measurable, Z_independent, Z_integrable, Z_mean_zero,
    fun i ω => (Y_hermitian i ω).sub (mean_hermitian i)⟩

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumSourceMatrixStructure

  let X : Fin d → Ω → Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ :=

steps.title: Preserve independence, integrability, zero mean and symmetry
steps.text: Apply joint independence preservation to the index-specific measurable maps A↦wiA. Fixed scalar multiplication preserves Bochner integrability and commutes with its integral, and real scalars preserve self-adjointness. None of these steps requires nonzero or positive weights. The two families are treated separately; no independence of their union is asserted.
steps.lean:
· exact hp.2.1.comp
      (fun i (A : Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1))
        (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ) => w i • A)
      (fun i => (measurable_const : Measurable
        (fun _ : Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1))
          (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ => w i)).smul measurable_id)
  · intro i
    exact (hp.2.2.1 i).smul (w i)
  · intro i
    dsimp only [X]
    rw [integral_smul, hp.2.2.2.1 i, smul_zero]
  · intro i ω
    exact (hp.2.2.2.2 i ω).smul (isSelfAdjoint_iff.mpr rfl)
